items.title: Show HN: Chatlo – an iOS-native AI agent, now with Jev
items.contentSnippet:
Hello HN!
I’m sure many of you have used AI agent apps like OpenClaw, Claude Code, or Codex on your PCs, but you rarely see AI agents running on the iOS platform. That’s why I created an agent app that runs exclusively on iOS—it doesn’t require a separate computer or server; it runs entirely on your iPhone.
Plus, in the latest version, we’ve become the first to integrate Jev AI—a very popular decision-making AI—on the App Store.
We invite you to try it out, and we look forward to your feedback.

items.title: The Creolisation of Recognition
items.contentSnippet: What if our recognition systems are still doing the quiet work of colonization, even when they claim inclusion? Simone Ravaioli of Instructure explores creolization as a generative framework for redesigning how we validate learning across cultural and epistemological borders. Drawing on thinkers like Tyson Yunkaporta and Serge Ravet, this piece challenges education leaders to move beyond Recognition of Prior Learning toward relational protocols that let different knowledge systems meet as equals

items.title: What Makes Dual Enrollment Actually Work: Robust Student & Family Support & Career Connection
items.contentSnippet: The third installment in our four-part series with Britebound moves beyond course design to ask a harder question: who is responsible when a student struggles? This post makes the case that robust dual enrollment requires named staff, early drop windows, family scaffolding, and mentors who open doors to careers students have never had reason to imagine. For district leaders building or scaling concurrent enrollment programs, this is the support infrastructure blueprint you have been looking for.
